BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                         OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy         )
Missouri Metro’s Request for Authority to Implement      )      File No. ER-2026-0143
a General Rate Increase for Electric Service             )

    STAFF OBJECTION TO NON-UNANIMOUS PARTIAL SETTLEMENT – RATE DESIGN

        COMES NOW the Staff (“Staff”) of the Missouri Public Service Commission

 (“Commission”), by and through counsel, and for its Objection to Non-Unanimous Partial

 Settlement – Rate Design respectfully states as follows:

        1.   On October 5, 2026, Evergy Missouri Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro

(“EMM”) and Midwest Energy Consumers Group (“MECG”) filed their Non-Unanimous Partial

Settlement – Rate Design (“Agreement”) resolving certain pending issues in this docket.

        2.   That same day, the Commission issued its Order Shortening Time to Object to

Stipulation and Agreements, directing the parties to file any objections no later than midnight

on October 7, 2026.

        3.   Pursuant to the Commission’s order and Commission Rule 20 CSR 4240-2.115,

Staff objects in part to the Agreement reached between EMM and MECG.

        4.   As counsel for Staff indicated in its general opening statement in this matter on

the afternoon of October 5, 2026, Staff does not object to restructuring of the EMM rates using

the “Bright Lines” proposed by EMM, the energy time periods proposed by EMM,

and a 15 minute on-peak demand measure as proposed by EMM, modified for a winter

demand measurement to begin at 7:00 am. Staff’s support of this rate structure, as modified,

is to enable EMM’s immediate work on a customer migration and determinants study, which

is necessary to calculate rates to be ordered in compliance tariffs in this case.

                                              1
            5.     Further discussion of specific objections, Staff’s recommendations for

    customer education, and Staff’s recommendations for the customer migration and

    determinants study are provided below.

                                        I.   Revenue Allocation

           6.     Staff objects to the Revenue Allocation detailed on page 2, paragraph 2 of the

    Agreement for the following reasons:

                a. The percentage adjustments indicated result in excessive total revenues when

                   applied to the settled-upon billing determinants;

                b. No reliable CCOS study is available in this case to support a result other than

                   an equal percentage increase to all classes. The CCOS studies relied upon by

                   EMM and MECG, among other things, misclassify distribution cost of service

                   such that the revenue responsibility of MGS, SGS, and Residential customers

                   is significantly overstated, and the revenue responsibility of LGS and LPS 1

                   customers is significantly understated. 2 Additionally, these results rely upon a

                   study approach that, among other concerns with the allocation of production-

                   related, energy-related, and transmission-related cost of service, has

                   Residential and Small business customers pay disproportionately for the cost

                   of owning renewable generation, while the largest customers benefit

                   disproportionately from the value of the energy generated, and from the

                   renewable energy credits generated; 3 and

             c. Staff objects to this stipulation’s result that LLPS rates be increased by a

               smaller percentage increase in this case than those applied to residential and

               small business customers.

              II.   Commercial and Industrial Rate Design – Implementation

       7.     Staff objects to the immediate implementation of new rates by bill cycle as

contemplated by the Agreement on page 2 for the following reasons:

            a. Immediate implementation will result in a rate increase and a significant

               change in rate structure in the peak winter billing months, without the benefit

               of any meaningful customer education.           This runs unnecessary and

               unreasonable risk of rate shock and customer disgruntlement, as opposed to

               providing an opportunity for customers to understand the purposes behind the

               pricing of the new rate structure, and to modify usage, if applicable,

               accordingly.

            b. This proposal was not brought forth until surrebuttal testimony, and no party

               has had an opportunity to address the impacts of its interaction with riders

               such as Fuel Adjustment Clause (“FAC”) and Missouri Energy Efficiency

               Investment Act (“MEEIA”) riders.

            c. Staff’s recommended customer education plan was provided in the Staff Rate

               Design Report beginning at page 27 and is attached for reference as

               Attachment A.

                               III.   Default Non-LLPS Rates

       8.     The Agreement contemplates, on page             3, increasing the      demand

component 1.25 times the class average assigned to the LPS/LGS classes, with the energy
                                              3
 component increasing 0.75, with the remainder of the class revenue requirement recovered

from the remaining rate elements. Staff objects to the demand and energy increases for the

following reasons:

          a. This change in intraclass revenue responsibility is arbitrary and may result in

             unreasonably low energy rates.

          b. The language is far too vague for implementation, and it is not clear what it

             actually applies to, in terms of (1) whether the adjustment applies on a class

             basis or on a subclass basis, and (2) whether the language refers to the exiting

             revenues by charge type, or EMM’s proposed rate revenues by charge type. If

             applied to EMM’s proposed rates, it does not address the intraclass and

             interclass continuity problems of EMM’s rate design; instead, it will exacerbate

             those problems. Further, EMM’s proposed rates were designed by EMM to

             collect the entire initially-requested revenue requirement. Increasing those

             rates, if that is what is contemplated in the stipulation, would be improper.

          c. The intraclass revenue responsibility modifications required by this language

             will undoubtably induce rate shock to customers not educated about the

             increases, compounded by the timing of the implementation of these rates

             contemplated in the stipulation.

          d. Without a customer migration and determinants study prior to implementation,

             there are no relevant determinants to use in calculating the applicable rates to

             result from this case. To be very clear – there are no determinants to calculate

             the rates EMM and MECG have stipulated to, and any attempt to rely on the

             factors and relationships that EMM provided in its direct testimony as applied
                                            4
               to the stipulated-to determinants is unreasonable and improper. Instead,

              EMM should be ordered to promptly complete a customer migration and

              determinants study based on the restructured rates and the time period

              of July 2025 – June 2026 to coincide with the current-class determinants that

              have been stipulated to by EMM and Staff in the Partial Stipulation and

              Agreement – Non-C&I Rate Design, filed on October 2, 2026. The Staff’s

              recommended customer migration and determinants study was provided in the

              Staff Rate Design Report beginning at page 24. Staff has included slight

              modifications in the version attached as Attachment B for consistency with the

              revisions to Staff’s positions related to accepting additional elements of the

              EMM-requested rate structure as modified by the Agreement.

       9.    Staff objects to the removal of reactive demand from Medium and Large General

service, as contemplated on page 3 of the Agreement, for the reasons stated in the rebuttal

testimony of Sarah Lange, beginning at page 68. Namely, with the changes in the regional

generation fleet, recovery of the cost of service associated with voltage stability is more

important, not less important.

       10.   Staff objects to the Agreement language on page 3 contemplating a review of

voltage of differentiated rates in the next EMM rate case because this review should happen

prior to the calculation of the rates and the implementation of the revised rate structure.

Implementation of the new rate structure should not occur without addressing this issue

consistent with Staff’s recommendations in its direct testimony concerning inter- and

intraclass pricing relationships, provided in the Staff Report at pages 32 – 39, modified to



                                            5
 reflect the time periods identified here-in. The unreasonable interclass results of the EMM

approach were discussed in the rebuttal testimony of Sarah Lange, and are illustrated below:




                                  IV.   Optional Time of Use

        11.   Staff objects to the incorporation of the high differential opt-in time-based rates

contemplated on page 3 of the Agreement as they are not cost-based and are poorly priced.

Staff further objects to incorporation of opt-in time-based rates absent a commitment

                                               6
     from EMM to not burden future cases with an attempt to recover revenues avoided by

    participating customers.

             12.   The Agreement contemplates on page 3 incorporating the resolving items from

    the standard rate. Staff agrees that if, against its objection, high differential opt-in time-based

    rates are made available, that the demand period for non-summer months and any energy

    pricing periods should be modified to avoid exacerbating winter morning peaks. Staff does

    not support application of the demand-energy pricing relationship described above to opt-in

    high differential time-based rates, if authorized by the Commission over Staff’s

    objections herein.

                                         V.     All Electric Rates

             13.   While Staff does not object to the elimination of all C&I electric rates as

    contemplated by the Agreement on page 3, Staff notes that if the Commission adopts Staff’s

    recommendation to delay the implementation of rate structure changes to outside of the

    peak winter months (and peak summer months), the all electric rates should remain available

    with an equal percentage increase until the restructured rates take effect.

                                              VI.   TRP 4 Rate

             14.   While Staff does not object to the freezing of the TRP rate for current customers

    in the non-residential class as contemplated on page 3 of the Agreement, Staff does object to

    increasing the components of this rate by 1.1 times the system average rate increase. Staff

    objects because this provision is being utilized to provide additional avoidance of applicable

    rate increases to LPS customers.




4
    Time Related Pricing

      WHEREFORE, Staff respectfully requests the Commission accept this objection and

reject the objected to portions of the Agreement reached between EMM and MECG.

                                          8
  Customer Education Recommendations

       Staff recommends that EMM inform its non-residential customers of the restructured

rates and provide reasonable education to those customers. This should include a

statement of the rate schedule the customer has been billed on, the rate schedule the

customer will be billed on, simple and clear education concerning the time-based periods

ordered in this case, an explanation of the recommended delay in restructuring until

November 2027, and a one-time report of the following:

       1. A statement of the total energy and 30-minute demand for 12 historic billing
          months,
       2. A statement of the total energy, energy by time-based period, 15-minute NCP
          demand, and 15 minute on-peak demand for the same 12 historic billing
          months,
       3. A calculation of the bill the customer would owe for the usage and demand for
          those 12 historic months on the increased non-restructured rates that are
          ordered in this case, and
       4. A calculation of the bill the customer would owe for the usage and demand for
          those 12 historic months on the restructured rates that are ordered in this case
          and effectuate the rate increase.
The Commission should also order EMM to test its billing system’s ability to accurately bill
the restructured rates, and to inform the Commission and the parties of any shortcomings
or delays in its ability to bill through a ﬁling in this docket.




                                                                                  Attachment A
 Customer Migration and Determinants Study Recommendation

         Staff recommends that customer migrations be established using the highest 15-

minute interval demand of the customers as it coincides with the on-peak demand period

for summer demand in EMM’s direct ﬁling, and the period for winter demand set out in the

Agreement which begins at 7:00 am.

         A reasonable sequence of a customer migration and determinants study is set out

below.

   1. Identify the applicable on-peak time interval and the applicable “Bright Lines”.

            a. Using 15-minute demands during the applicable seasonal demand periods.

            b. Using EMM’s selection of the 31 MW, 250 MW, and 3,000 MW thresholds as

                “Bright Lines.”

   2. Find the 15-minute on-peak demand of each customer for each of the 12 historic

         billing months. Determine which restructured rate class the customer should be

         served under based on that customer’s 15-minute on-peak demand and the selected

         “Bright Lines.”

   3. For each restructured class, calculate the monthly determinants for each charge, as

         the sum of the determinants of the customers migrated to that restructured class

         based on 15-minute on-peak demand:

            a. Customer charge determinants,

            b. 15-minute facilities demand, by service voltage, and as applicable, billing

                block,




                                                                               Attachment B
 c. 15-minute on peak billing demand, including minimum demands, by service

   voltage,

d. Reactive demand,

e. Total energy, by service voltage, and

f. Energy by time period, consistent with EMM’s direct-ﬁled energy time periods,

   by service voltage.
